title: Immunoprecipitation/Pull-down of ATP6AP1-FLAG in HEK293 WT cells treated with and without a mitochondrial translation inhibitor
projectDescription: Dataset: HEK293 WT cells were transfected with ATP6AP1-FLAG expression vector for 96h, with or without the presence of 15uM actinonin, a mitochondrial translation inhibitor. Immunoprecipitation was performed using FLAG antibody and Protein-G Sepharose, and the samples were analysed with label-free whole cell proteomics
sampleProcessingProtocol: The IP beads were dissolved in 50mM ammonium bicarbonate, reduced, alkylated and digested with trypsin (1:50 enzyme : protein ratio; Promega) at 37 degree for overnight.  For immunoprecipitation (IP) experiments proteins after IP were dissolved in 50mM ammonium bicarbonate, reduced, alkylated and on-beads digested with 1ug trypsin (Promega) at 37 degree for overnight.  Before LC-MS/MS digested peptides were acidified and desalted by homemade C18 stage tips. LC MS was carried with timsTOF PRO2 (Bruker) coupled to nanoElute (Bruker). The timsTOF Pro2 mass spectrometer was operated in DIA-PASEF mode. Mass spectra for MS were recorded between m/z 100 and 1700. Ion mobility resolution was set to 0.85–1.30 V·s/cm over a ramp time of 100 ms.  The MS/MS mass range was limited to m/z 475-1000 and ion mobility resolution to 0.85-1.27 V s/cm to exclude singly changed ions.  The estimated cycle time was 0.95 s with 8 cylces using DIA windows of 25 Da. Collisional energy was ramped from 20eV at 0.60 V s/cm to 59eV at 1.60 V s/cm.
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS analysis was carried out with a nanoElute LC coupled to a timsTOF PRO2 mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonics), with a Captive Spray nano electrospray ion source (Bruker Daltonics). The mass spectrometer was operated in PASEF mode. Whole cell lysates were analysed using data dependent acquisition and IP samples using data independent acquisition. Raw files from LC-MS/MS analyses were submitted to DIA-NN, version 1.9.1 using the library-free function (IP samples) for protein identification and label-free quantification. LC-MS/MS data quality evaluation and statistical analysis was done using software Perseus ver 1.6.15.0
